title: Hodges fills in for Ellington and Holmes stays with Russell
summary: Ellington's trouble with Otto Hardwick put Hodges in his band while Webb idled, and Holmes preferred the steady work with Russell.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well, that's I think the first time... I think that's the first time I turned down Duke Ellington. Because at that time, he was having trouble with Otto, Johnny hadn't joined the band. He had tried to get Johnny; Johnny was with Chick...
Now, this Nest thing was after you'd made that ten-place gig in New England.
You did go with Chick Webb, and on your return...
Yeah. Now I've come back to the Nest, because Chick's not doing anything. I'm still with Chick.
I'm still with Chick's band. I'm rehearsing every day, even though I'm working at the Nest.

Well, I worked and worked and worked at the Nest. And in the meantime, Duke was having trouble with Otto Hardwick, and... Then that's how he got Johnny in the band! Because he was having trouble with Otto. Well, Johnny wasn't doin' nothin', and so Johnny went to fill in with Duke until Chick gets something to do -- same as me!

Well, Chick was so long getting anything, that when it was time for him to come out of there, Johnny was so well implanted in Duke's band he wouldn't let him go. And I wasn't thinkin' about leaving Russell's band to go back to Chick, because Chick couldn't stay on work...he didn't work that long. He'd get on a job, he'd have good bands. But I can't pay the rent talkin' about "I work in Chick Webb's band"!
